binders: n is an arbitrary natural number, and Fin n is the common row and column index set.
B is an arbitrary real n by n matrix, represented by B : Fin n -> Fin n -> Real.
q is an arbitrary sequence of real n-vectors indexed by natural-number time steps.
d is an arbitrary sequence of real n-vectors indexed by natural-number time steps.
s is an arbitrary fixed real n-vector.
In the conclusion, m is an arbitrary natural number and i is an arbitrary element of Fin n.
There are no existentially quantified objects or witnesses.
hypotheses: For every i,j in Fin n, B(i,j) >= 0.
For every i in Fin n, s(i) >= 0.
For every natural number t and every i in Fin n, |d_t(i)| <= s(i).
For every natural number t and every i in Fin n, q_{t+1}(i) = sum over j in Fin n of B(i,j)q_t(j) + d_t(i).
conclusions: For every natural number m and every i in Fin n, |q_{m+1}(i)| <= sum over j in Fin n of (B^(m+1))(i,j)|q_0(j)| + sum from k = 0 through m of the sum over j in Fin n of (B^k)(i,j)s(j).
mathematical_definitions: For a vector x, (A x)(i) means sum over j in Fin n of A(i,j)x(j).
For matrices A and C, (A C)(i,j) means sum over k in Fin n of A(i,k)C(k,j).
I(i,j) is 1 if i = j and 0 otherwise.
The powers used here are defined by B^0 = I and B^(r+1) = B B^r.
The vector |q_0| is componentwise: its j-th component is |q_0(j)|.
The accumulated sum over Finset.range(m+1) is exactly the sum over k = 0,1,...,m.
Equivalently, the right-hand side is (B^(m+1)|q_0|)(i) + sum from k = 0 through m of (B^k s)(i).
translation.proposition_plain_english: Given an entrywise nonnegative real square matrix B, a vector sequence satisfying the exact recurrence q_{t+1} = Bq_t + d_t, and perturbations whose components are uniformly bounded in absolute value by a fixed nonnegative vector s, every component of q after m+1 steps is bounded in absolute value by the corresponding component of B^(m+1)|q_0| plus the accumulated componentwise bound sum_{k=0}^m B^k s.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The dimension n may be zero. When n = 0, Fin n has no elements, so all indexwise hypotheses and the universally indexed conclusion are vacuous.
The statement is conditional and gives no conclusion for data that fail any of the four hypotheses.
B is fixed across all time steps and must be entrywise nonnegative; no result is encoded for matrices with negative entries.
The perturbation bound s is fixed and independent of time, although d_t may vary arbitrarily with t.
The result is componentwise and uses scalar absolute values; it does not state a vector-norm or matrix-norm inequality.
All quantities and operations are over exact real numbers. No floating-point format, rounding operation, unit roundoff, relative-error model, or computed-versus-exact distinction is encoded.
No assumptions such as symmetry, invertibility, stochasticity, bounded norm, or contractivity of B are present.
No convergence, asymptotic stability, optimality, sharpness, or lower bound is asserted.
The initial vector q_0 is unrestricted.
The conclusion holds for every natural-number time m, with no finite time horizon.
